source_text:
Μνημονεύετε ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν τῆς ἐν Συρίᾳ ἐκκλησίας, ἥτις ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ ποιμένι τῷ θεῷ χρῆται. μόνος αὐτὴν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐπισκοπήσει καὶ ἡ ὑμῶν ἀγάπη.
ἐγὼ δὲ αἰσχύνομαι ἐξ αὐτῶν λέγεσθαι: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἄξιός εἰμι, ὣν ἔσχατος αὐτῶν καὶ ἔκτρωμα: ἀλλ’ ἠλέημαί τις εἶναι, ἐὰν θεοῦ ἐπιτύχω.
ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν τῶν δεξαμένων με εἰς ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, οὐχ ὡς παροδεύοντα. καὶ γὰρ αἱ μὴ προσήκουσαί μοι τῇ ὁδῷ τῇ κατὰ σάρκα, κατὰ πόλιν με προῆγον.
thought_title: Remember the Syrian church in prayer
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Ephesians, asking them to pray for the church in Syria and reflecting on his own unworthiness.
pass_a_gloss: Remember in your prayer the church in Syria, which instead of me uses God as shepherd. Alone Jesus Christ will oversee it and your love. But I am ashamed to be called from among them: for I am not even worthy, being last of them and an untimely birth: but I have been shown mercy to be someone, if I attain God. My spirit greets you and the love of the churches that received me in the name of Jesus Christ, not as one passing through. For even the churches not belonging to me in the way according to flesh, city by city went before me.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the dative of means with χρῆται; the church in Syria has God as its shepherd in place of Ignatius
Future tense of ἐπισκοπέω; the glossary reserves 'bishop' for the noun ἐπίσκοπος, so the verb is rendered literally as 'oversee'
Literal sense of a miscarriage or premature birth, used self-deprecatingly; echoes Paul's use in 1 Corinthians 15:8
Perfect passive of ἐλεέω, emphasizing the state of having received mercy

choices.english: in the way according to flesh
choices.why: Literal rendering of the dative of respect with ὁδός; 'according to flesh' is a fixed Pauline phrase kept literal

choices.english: city by city went before me
choices.why: Literal distributive use of κατά with accusative; προῆγον is imperfect, indicating repeated action along the journey
rejected: preceded me from city to city
went ahead of me in each city

pass_b_english: Remember in your prayers the church in Syria, which now has God as its shepherd in my place. Jesus Christ alone will be its bishop, and your love will watch over it.

As for me, I am ashamed to be counted among them, for I am not worthy. I am the last of them and an untimely birth, as Paul said of himself. But I have been shown mercy to be someone, if I attain to God.

My spirit greets you, and so does the love of the churches that welcomed me in the name of Jesus Christ, not as one merely passing through. Even the churches that were not on my route according to the flesh escorted me ahead from city to city.

problems.quote: Jesus Christ alone will oversee it, along with your love.
problems.source_quote: μόνος αὐτὴν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐπισκοπήσει καὶ ἡ ὑμῶν ἀγάπη
problems.why: ἐπισκοπήσει is future indicative, not 'oversee'; glossary bans 'overseer' for ἐπίσκοπος root. Also 'alone' (μόνος) modifies Christ, but 'along with your love' creates contradiction.
problems.fix: Jesus Christ alone will be its bishop, and your love.
problems.ruling: ἐπισκοπήσει means 'will visit/attend to,' not 'oversee'; μόνος + καὶ ἡ ὑμῶν ἀγάπη is contradictory ('alone...along with').

problems.quote: Yet I have been shown mercy, if only I attain to God.
problems.source_quote: ἀλλ’ ἠλέημαι τις εἶναι, ἐὰν θεοῦ ἐπιτύχω
problems.why: τις εἶναι is omitted; it means 'to be someone' (worthwhile). 'Yet' adds contrast not in ἀλλά here.
problems.fix: But I have been shown mercy to be someone, if I attain to God.
problems.ruling: τις εἶναι ('to be someone/something') is omitted, changing meaning; 'if only' misrepresents ἐὰν ἐπιτύχω ('if I attain').

problems.quote: went before me from city to city
problems.why: προῆγον means 'led me forth/escorted me ahead,' not 'went before me'; agency reversed.
problems.fix: escorted me ahead from city to city
problems.ruling: προῆγον με = 'led/escorted me'; English 'went before me' reverses agency, omitting με as object.

edits.old: Jesus Christ alone will oversee it, along with your love.
edits.new: Jesus Christ alone will be its bishop, and your love.

edits.old: Yet I have been shown mercy, if only I attain to God.
edits.new: But I have been shown mercy to be someone, if I attain to God.

edits.old: went before me from city to city
edits.new: escorted me ahead from city to city

last_rejected.quote: not as one merely passing through
last_rejected.why: English adds 'merely' which weakens the negation; source says 'not as one passing through' period, emphasizing genuine welcome vs. casual reception.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Merely passing through' fairly renders παροδεύοντα; 'merely' is a minor addition, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: προσήκουσαι means 'belonging/pertaining to,' not 'on my route.' The churches didn't belong to his road, i.e., weren't situated along his way.
last_rejected.fix: did not lie on my road
last_rejected.ruling: 'On my route' adequately conveys προσήκουσαι τῇ ὁδῷ; 'belonging to the road' and 'on route' overlap in meaning.

polish.changed: Clarified that 'your love' will watch over the Syrian church, made the pronoun references explicit, and broke long sentences into natural modern rhythm while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Same Greek presbyterion rendered with and without parenthetical 'presbyters', risking confusion.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note.

notes.quote: council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles
notes.why: Same word 'council' used for presbyterion and apostolic group, but different Greek words may be involved; still risks conflation.
notes.fix: Note Greek terms or use 'college of apostles' if distinct.

polish.changed: Clarified the allusion to Paul's self-description in 1 Corinthians 15:8, made the speaker and pronouns explicit, and smoothed the sentence flow for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Echoes 1 Corinthians 15:8 (Paul's self-description); reader may miss the allusion.
